_spec.purpose: The automation-change trail. Every machine upgrade a run makes to itself.
_spec.why: A routine whose last phase edits its own machine will drift, and the drift is invisible unless each change is written down where the next run and the maintainer both see it. Each set reverts as one commit.
_spec.bound_by: ownership.yaml. An upgrade needing another actor's files is not an upgrade this run gets to make; it is written here as a proposal and stops.

_shape.why_entries_is_empty: The `entries` array above is empty and will stay empty. ownership.yaml marks this path append_only, and ownership_check implements that as 'the diff contains no removed line'. Adding the first element to a JSON array moves its closing bracket, which rewrites the line `"entries": []`, so the array could never receive an entry and the rule refused the operation it exists to permit. Nothing had ever written this file, so nothing had ever found out.
_shape.how_to_append: One top level key per run date, with the COMMA LEADING on its own line, inserted immediately before the final closing brace. That is the only JSON shape that grows by pure insertion: the previous entry's closing brace is untouched because its separator lives on the next line, and the file's last line never moves. Read it with json.load and take every key that parses as a date.
_shape.the_rule_was_not_loosened: ownership.yaml was not edited and could not be: it belongs to the human actor. The shape moved to fit the rule rather than the rule moving to fit the shape.

The occlusion probe compares text to OPAQUE ELEMENT BOXES four or more px in both dimensions, and this rule painted BENEATH the footnote anyway. glyph_ink_contamination fires on ink of the glyphs' OWN value and the rule was a different colour on the same sheet. busy_art_under_text measures edge DENSITY, and one clean rule through a line is the lowest density structure there is. Every gate answered its own question correctly. The scorer found it by reading render_report.json's coordinates by hand at the ship gate, where a repair costs a rebuild.

every_quantity_and_where_it_came_from.the glyph band: the em box centred in the measured line box, which is CSS's own content area for an inline box. Derived from the node's own font-size and its rendered line box, so nothing is typed and it scales with the type. Half leading falls outside it, which is what separates a rule THROUGH a word from a rule sitting in the gap under it.
every_quantity_and_where_it_came_from.rule or plate: the strip's thickness must be under one em of the struck type. At one em or more the thing is a plate and the occlusion probe already owns plates. One em is the type's own unit.
every_quantity_and_where_it_came_from.how much crossed: a horizontal rule must cross at least one em of the line, so a clipped corner is not a strike. A vertical rule must stand at least one em inside both ends of the line box, because a column divider brushing the end of a line box is ordinary and a vertical rule inside a run of words is not.
every_quantity_and_where_it_came_from.can a reader see it: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11's 3.0:1 non-text contrast floor, MEASURED off the PNG between the strip's worst scan line and the paper beside it. An external published standard, so it cannot ratchet the way a figure derived from our own corpus would. Under it the strip is the quiet divider GATE_LESSONS 7 says is allowed to be quiet, and this gate says nothing about it.
every_quantity_and_where_it_came_from.paint order: deliberately not consulted, and that is not an oversight. The rule that shipped painted under the footnote and read as a strikethrough regardless.

not_reached_and_why.proposal_11, a relationship between sour: This was ranked second by the phase that launched me and I did not build it, because I could not build a version I could demonstrate failing. The defect is exact: slide 6 printed `260 MW load + 265.5 MW generation`, guarded by an assertion in compute.py that the components equal the quoted 525.5. A tautology cannot fail, so it certifies nothing. The proposed cure is a related(cid, ...) in compute.py that asks a claim rather than asking arithmetic. THE REASON IT IS STILL A PROPOSAL: compute.py is written fresh by the model every run and has no template file in any lane, so there is nowhere in scripts/ or .claude/ to put related(). The one seat that exists is aggregates.json, whose declaration format already carries quoted_from and from_claims, and a `kind: relation` entry requiring a claim id whose quote states the relation would be the bounded version. I could not write a self-test that distinguishes a true relation from a false one on this deck's own data, because 265.5 legitimately IS a generation figure under c3 AND legitimately IS the Crusoe One Load in the recital, which is GATE_LESSONS 20's shape: a true figure attached to the wrong population. frontier_scan.focus: span-level and pinpoint-citation verification, chosen because it is the class this run paid for
frontier_scan.the_finding_that_most_justifies_locator_: Is this Citation on Point? (arXiv 2608.12571) corrupts legal citations at three difficulties and measures whether a model catches it. Replacing the whole cited case: 93 to 100 percent recall. Changing ONLY the pinpoint page within the same case: 37 to 61 percent. The paper's conclusion is that models recognise the right legal topic without verifying support for the cited proposition. LePhantomCite (arXiv 2606.21155) reports the same asymmetry: AI reliably detects non-existent cases and name mismatches and struggles with pincites. A pinpoint locator is the single hardest thing for a reading model to check and one of the easiest things for a set-membership test to check, which is the argument for taking it off the judges and giving it to a gate.
frontier_scan.the_finding_that_names_proposal_11: Not Wrong, But Untrue: LLM Overconfidence in Document-Based Queries (arXiv 2509.25498) names the failure as interpretive overreach: rather than inventing facts, models make analytical claims the documents did not support. That is exactly `260 load + 265.5 generation`, where every ingredient was sourced and the relation was not. It also shows why the obvious method would not have caught it: CLATTER (arXiv 2506.05243) decomposes a sentence into sub-facts and entails each one, and BOTH sub-facts here entail. A decomposition-and-aggregate checker PASSES this sentence. The relation needs a claim of its own, not a finer decomposition.
frontier_scan.the_generalisable_idea_worth_keeping: Hardware assertion-based verification has a name for the palette regex defect. An assertion A |-> B passes VACUOUSLY when A never becomes true, and the standard remedy is a COVER PROPERTY on the antecedent, asserted separately, so a suite can tell 'never violated' from 'never exercised'. Every gate in this repo that selects what to examine should carry one. GATE_LESSONS 26 already has half of it, where text_contrast prints the count it declined on success as well as on failure. Both gates touched this run now carry one: plan_render_check asserts every shipped storyboard yields at least five palette tokens, and locator_trace asserts the newest deck yields more than zero locator tokens.
frontier_scan.an_external_threshold_for_proposal_9_so_: The CIE gives the number this project would otherwise have had to measure off its own corpus, which the threshold rule in GATE_LESSONS warns is a ratchet. CIEDE2000 dE00 near 1.0 is a just noticeable difference, 2 to 3 is perceptible on close observation, above 5 is clearly visible. Computed here for the three collisions round 3's craft judge named against deck no. 8: satin_spar #F5F1E6 against cut_face #F4F0E4 is dE00 0.49, caliche_cap #E4DCC6 against limestone #E5DECC is 1.52, and ledge_shadow #241E22 against blackland #211E1A is 6.49. So two of the judge's three are at or under the JND and the third is a genuinely different colour, which is the case for measuring rather than eyeballing, in both directions. satin_spar at 0.49 is the deck's declared light and its type colour across nine frames, so the most-seen colour in deck no. 10 is deck no. 8's light under a new name, and no eye could have told you which of the three mattered.

frontier_scan.focus: layout faults invisible to DOM assertions, and identifier-level citation verification. Both were chosen because they are the two classes this run paid for, in rounds 4 and 5.
frontier_scan.the_finding_that_most_justifies_numeral_: CiteAudit (arXiv 2602.23452) names the exact failure mode as its own category, Identifier Fabrication, and describes it in a sentence that could have been written about round 4: an identifier resolves to a real work, but the visible citation text describes a different one. Its own note is that these are hard to detect through surface-level similarity because the citation appears structurally complete while being invalid, which is why copy_sync_check passed. Its dataset is 6,475 real and 2,967 fake citations and the fakes include DOI and identifier hallucinations specifically because they cannot be caught by text similarity alone. HALLMARK (arXiv 2607.18360) diagnoses three failure modes in citation verifiers and is the paper to read before widening the authorised set here.
frontier_scan.how_that_changed_the_design: It is the argument for checking the NUMBER against the cited claim rather than checking that the claim exists. This repo already had the second, in copy_sync_check, and had it since 2026-08-12. The gap between them is exactly the gap the benchmark measures.
frontier_scan.the_finding_that_most_justifies_the_furn: ReDeCheck and the responsive layout literature behind it (Walsh, Software Testing Verification and Reliability, 2020, and the SIGSOFT ISSTA 2017 tool paper) detect layout failures WITHOUT AN EXPLICIT ORACLE by building a Responsive Layout Graph and comparing alignment constraints across renderings, rather than by asserting absolute geometry. The failures it names are elements protruding, overlapping, or INCORRECTLY WRAPPING TO THE NEXT LINE, which is this run's foot row named in the literature's own words. The design consequence is the one taken above: the comparison is the oracle, so no threshold has to be typed.
frontier_scan.the_thing_worth_knowing_that_was_not_use: The 2026 industry writing on visual regression is unanimous that DOM assertions are structurally incapable of seeing truncated text and layout shift, and unanimous that the answer is a vision model comparing screenshots. That is a real technique and it is the wrong one here. A screenshot diff has no opinion about which difference matters, and this product's whole design is that the art varies every run, so a pixel comparison between decks would be noise from the first frame. Comparing a deck against ITSELF, frame to frame, over the parts that are supposed to be identical, is the same idea with a subject narrow enough to be an oracle.

frontier_scan.focus: constraint induced collapse of output variety, and conflict between two instructions given to one writer. Chosen because that is the class this run paid for, seven times.
frontier_scan.the_finding_that_most_justifies_the_capt: ConInstruct (arXiv 2511.14342) benchmarks whether models detect conflicting constraints and what they do about them. Detection is strong, 87.3 F1 for Claude 4.5 Sonnet and 91.5 for DeepSeek R1, and the paper's headline is that models 'rarely explicitly notify users about the conflicts or request clarification when faced with conflicting constraints'. They resolve them silently. That is this defect exactly. The caption room met the refusal, resolved it by switching to the close that passes, and said nothing, seven runs running, and the fix that follows is not better detection. It is making the resolution stated where the next writer reads it, which is what the message and the doctrine section now do.
frontier_scan.the_second_finding: Evaluating the Diversity and Quality of LLM Generated Content (arXiv 2504.12522) argues for EFFECTIVE semantic diversity, meaning diversity measured only among outputs that clear a quality threshold, because diversity without quality is trivial. Read the other way round it is the warning this run needed. A variety ledger that records what was used without recording what was AVAILABLE under the constraints in force will report a healthy menu while one option is the only legal one. That is the argument for the doctrine marking the fifth substance unavailable rather than leaving five names on a list.
frontier_scan.the_third: Work on n-gram novelty finds that more constrained decoding strategies decrease novelty, which is the mechanism here in one sentence and is worth remembering the next time a hard form rule is added to any surface. Ask what it costs the variety ledger on the day it is written.
frontier_scan.not_pursued: Verbalized Sampling and the geometric mode collapse regulators are about sampling inside a model and there is nothing in this pipeline to apply them to. The caption is written by an agent under a brief, and the lever here is the brief and the ledger.
